title: The Speaking Oak and the Building of the Argo

scope.description: The Speaking Oak instructs Jason and the Argo is built with a speaking figurehead.
scope.boundaryRationale: The source heading and two narrative paragraphs form the ship-building setup before later voyage episodes.

sourceBoundaryDecision: The source heading and two narrative paragraphs form the ship-building setup before later voyage episodes.

evidence.sourceText: When Jason, sobered and refreshed by a long night's rest, perceived how foolish had been his vow, he would fain have recalled it; but, mindful of Chiron's teachings ever to be true to his word, he resolved to depart for Colchis.
To secure Juno's assistance, he began by visiting her shrine at Dodona, where the oracle, a Speaking Oak, assured him of the goddess's good will and efficacious protection.

Next the Speaking Oak bade him cut off one of its own mighty limbs, and carve from it a figurehead for the swift-sailing vessel which Minerva, at Juno's request, would build for his use from pine trees grown on Mount Pelion.

When quite completed, Jason called his vessel the Argo (swift-sailing), and speedily collected a crew of heroes as brave as himself, among whom were Hercules, Castor, Pollux, Peleus, Admetus, Theseus, and Orpheus, who were all glad to undertake the perilous journey to lands unknown.
